title: Coming home; records, Earl Hines and James P. Johnson
summary: He heard records his sister brought home and talks about Hines, Armstrong and James P. Johnson.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: When you came back to New Orleans, you didn't start playing music right away? No, I learned how to play ukulele. Did you used to go around and listen to bands here? No. You must have been about 19.

You see, my sister used to work for Nashville, Albany and St. Charles, she worked for the family of Wilberforce had the music store. And Franklin Burr, he was singing then, the man he called Perry Mason. You understand what I mean? And he was singing, he used to sing that on records. And she used to bring all them records home and things like that. And she started bringing a lot of records home, and I ain't got nobody, you know Bobby himself playing piano and stuff like that. He come from Pittsburgh and he got into Chicago and Louis formed up a band and branched off from Oliver and formed up his own band where he got Earl Hines. Earl Hines in Admiral's style, where he got all them the menaces and things that Louis was making. He knew music. See James P. Johnson taught Earl Hines and he taught, James P. Johnson taught Vatwiler too, yeah. Vatwiler was a piano player, but James P. Johnson and those fellas, he had Liotta Lyon, but Liotta Lyon he never did want to learn the music. He used to play all that close harmony. You understand what I mean? He'd smoke them big cigars and things like that. And old P. Johnson would be there now he could make you laugh. P. Johnson went down there in the village and he said I'm going to dedicate this number to a little Creole boy from there. Oh you know him? You married him too? Liotta Lyon?
